title.narrative: Our Rights, Our Lives, Our Future (O3) Malawi PhaseII - Royal Norwegian Embassy

description.narrative:
The Our Rights, Our Lives, Our Future (O3) Malawi project, with the support from Norway, will benefit Malawi in six education divisions: Northern Education Division (NED); Central East Education Division (CEED); Central West Education Division (CWED); South East Education Division; Shire Highlands Education Division (SHED) and South West Education Division (SWED).
Deliberate steps to deepen the quality and build strong foundations for education for health and well-being at primary school level will be taken. Foundational Education for Health and Well Being (FEHW) supports learners to develop transferable skills that are vital for foundational learning, such as decision-making, social and emotional skills, communication skills, critical thinking and problem-solving skills, among others. Good quality Life Skills based sexuality education curricula is underpinned by the following principles: age- and developmentally appropriate, scientifically accurate, holistic, human rights-based, inclusive, transformative and relevant to the context and culture (UNESCO et al., 2018; UNICEF, 2019).
Sexuality education is most effective when delivered as part of a whole-school approach to health and well-being. This means that the curriculum is positioned within an ecosystem that includes supportive school management, safe and healthy school environments, engagement with parents and communities, linkages with child- and adolescent-responsive health and social services and well-trained and supported teachers. Good quality health education is delivered through learner-centred pedagogical approaches, accompanied by appropriate teaching and learning materials and is inclusive of learners in all of their diversity.
To strengthen the quality of teacher training and bring the training closer to school level, Phase 2 will introduce a model for training primary school teachers using Colleges of Education as a central point. Selected Colleges of Education - Domasi and Chiradzulu in the Southern Region, Lilongwe in the Central Region and Rumphi and Mzuzu University in the North, will be focus points of training of teachers in 4 education divisions. These centres will be used as hubs for bringing together all elements of the O3 programme; in-service teacher training; pre-service teacher training; teacher continuous professional development; monitoring and support supervision; community engagement and linkages with adolescent friendly health services.
The O3 project will continue to support government’s commitment to strengthen child protection and end school-related gender-based violence to ensure care and support for teaching and learning through provision of curriculum-based, age-appropriate SRHR information and comprehensive sexuality education to female and male learners and expose them to role models to enable them to stay in school.
As part of building the quality of CSE that primary school learners receive, the O3 project will work with the Ministry of Education to ensure that learners who are over-age in the lower classes are provided with information and skills to make healthy choices. Seeing that learners who are over-age are mainly in foundational classes, the programme will ensure that these learners have access to basic sexuality education along with standard-age learners. This will be achieved through the enhancement of the primary school teacher training.
